item.title: Treasury Yields, Fed Rate-Hike Bets Rise After Strong U.S. Jobs Data
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury yields jump after significantly stronger-than-expected employment data for August lifted expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the Sept. 16 meeting.

item.title: Soft Retail Sales Reveal Cracks in Eurozone Resilience to Energy Shock
item.content:encoded: Eurozone retail sales fell unexpectedly in July, a sign that the currency area’s resilience in the face of high energy prices might be faltering even as separate figures pointed to a continued recovery in German industry.

item.title: BOE Survey Points to Cooling Price Pressures
item.content:encoded: Businesses expect the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, a decrease from the 3.9% expected in July.

item.title: Swiss Inflation Jumps on Higher Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: Swiss inflation jumped in August, reversing several months of cooling price growth as renewed tensions in the Middle East pushed global energy costs higher.

item.title: Global Bond Yields Surge as Oil Prices Fuel Inflation Worries
item.content:encoded: Global bond yields surged as renewed tension between the U.S. and Iran reinforced inflation expectations, which increased the prospect of interest-rate hikes in the coming months.

item.title: German Inflation Rises But Few Signs of Energy-Shock Spillover
item.content:encoded: Inflation picked up in Germany this month, though less than expected, with few signs of broader price pressures in the economy despite conflict in the Middle East keeping upward pressure on energy costs.

item.title: U.S. Home Price Growth Rose in June
item.content:encoded: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index rose 1.5% in the 12 months through June, compared with a 1.2% increase in May.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Dropped in July
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell sharply below expectations in July as home-builder sentiment remained muted.

item.title: The Dutch central bank said it moved around 86 metric tons of gold from New York and Ottawa to London as a result of “increasing geopolitical unrest”
item.content:encoded: The Dutch central bank said shifting the 78 metric tons of gold, worth $11 billion, would improve its ability to trade the metal in a pinch.

item.title: Malaysia Central Bank Holds Rates as Growth Stays Firm
item.content:encoded: Malaysia’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, as expected, as strong economic growth and mild inflation gave policymakers room to remain on hold.

item.title: U.S. Services-Sector Activity Expanded Again in August
item.content:encoded: The Institute for Supply Management’s purchasing managers index for services providers was 55.4 in August compared with 54.1 in July.

item.title: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans
item.content:encoded: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Has Dropped in August, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: Consumers’ economic mood is weaker this month versus July, according to preliminary results from the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

item.title: Retail Sales Fell Last Month
item.content:encoded: Retailers’ sales fell by 0.6% last month to $763.6 billion, versus the 0.2% growth recorded in June.

item.title: Eurozone Retail Sales Retreat as Consumers Still Fret Over War
item.content:encoded: Retail sales in the eurozone fell in June and was the second decline in the four full months since the start of the war against Iran.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Rose in July, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index rose to 55.2 from 49.5 in June as gasoline prices cooled.

item.title: U.S. Trade Deficit Widened in July
item.content:encoded: U.S. imports were higher than exports by $88.6 billion, versus $71.2 billion in June. Analysts polled were expecting a $90 billion deficit.

item.title: Capital Account: Under his “Donroe” doctrine, President Trump no longer treats Venezuela as sovereign. Canada fears the same treatment, @greg_ip writes.
item.content:encoded: Under his “Donroe” doctrine, President Trump no longer treats Venezuela as sovereign. Canada fears the same treatment.

item.title: South Korea’s Exports Extend Chip-Led Growth in August
item.content:encoded: Semiconductors, which account for more than a third of South Korea’s exports by value this year, continued to drive the gains.

item.title: Many small and medium-sized Canadian business owners expect to bear the brunt of the Trump administration’s tariffs
item.content:encoded: Honey, cosmetic and other exporters now face 50% levies.
